meta.title: About — Free Construction Calculators & Contractor Software
meta.description: About iHateConstruction — free construction calculators for cement, concrete, brick, steel, paint, and tile, plus BOQ, quotation, and GST invoicing built for Indian contractors.

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Construction in India is a ₹13 lakh crore industry — and most contractors still estimate costs on paper, send quotations via WhatsApp screenshots, and track payments in a notebook. The tools that exist are either built for American general contractors (Procore, Buildertrend) or too complex for a 5-person team doing residential work.
items: Guessing material quantities → over-ordering by 15-20% (₹ straight into the drain)
Quoting from memory → missing items, underpricing, awkward conversations later
Tracking payments on paper → "Did they pay the second installment or not?"
Sharing documents → WhatsApp forwards of blurry PDFs made in MS Paint

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: iHateConstruction gives Indian contractors a single place to estimate, quote, invoice, and get paid — without the enterprise bloat or the $300/month price tag.

calculators.title: Calculators

meta.title: Privacy Policy — How We Handle Your Data
meta.description: iHateConstruction privacy policy. Learn what personal data we collect, how we use it, where it's stored, and your rights over your account, projects, calculations, and business data.

s1.heading: 1. Information We Collect
s1.intro: When you use iHateConstruction, we collect:

items.rest: Name, email address, and authentication credentials (managed via Clerk).
Projects, calculations, materials, BOQs, quotations, and invoices you create.
Pages visited, features used, browser type, device info, and IP address.
UPI IDs and QR codes you voluntarily upload. We do not process or store credit card numbers.

s2.heading: 2. How We Use Your Data
items: Provide, maintain, and improve the service.
Generate documents (BOQs, quotations, invoices, PDFs) as you request.
Send transactional emails (account verification, password resets).
Analyze usage patterns to improve features (aggregated, never sold).

s3.heading: 3. Data Storage & Security
s3.body: Your data is stored in encrypted databases hosted on secure cloud infrastructure. We use TLS for all data in transit. Authentication is handled by Clerk, a SOC 2 Type II compliant provider.

s4.heading: 4. Data Sharing
s4.intro: We do not sell your data. We share data only with:

items.rest: Hosting (Vercel), authentication (Clerk), database (managed PostgreSQL) — only what's necessary for operations.
When you generate a public quotation link, the quotation details are visible to anyone with the link.
If required by Indian law or valid court order.
View all data associated with your account.
Download your projects, calculations, and documents.
Request complete deletion of your account and all associated data.
Update inaccurate information at any time.

s6.heading: 6. Cookies
s6.body: We use essential cookies for authentication and session management. No advertising cookies. No third-party tracking pixels.

s7.heading: 7. Data Retention
s7.body: Your data is retained as long as your account is active. Deleted accounts are purged within 30 days. Audit logs are retained for 1 year for security purposes.

s8.heading: 8. Children
s8.body: iHateConstruction is not intended for users under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from minors.

s9.heading: 9. Changes

sizes.heading: Rebar sizes

article.heading: Everything you need to know about rebar

faq.q: How much rebar do I need for a concrete slab?
faq.a: Enter the slab length and width, the centre-to-centre spacing, and the edge cover. The calculator returns the bars in each direction, the total rebar length in metres, and the number of stock bars (12 m) to order. A 6 × 4 m slab at 150 mm c/c needs roughly 66 bars and about 306 m of rebar.

faq.q: How do I calculate rebar for a slab in square feet?
faq.a: Find the slab area in square feet, divide by the spacing on each side to get the bar lines, then multiply by the bar length. The calculator does this for you and also reports rebar weight per square foot — a typical single-layer residential mesh works out to roughly 1 kg per sq ft.

faq.q: How do I calculate rebar weight?
faq.a: Rebar weight = total length × weight per metre. For diameter D in millimetres, weight per metre ≈ D² / 162 kg/m (from π × (D/2)² × 7850 kg/cum). A 12 mm bar weighs about 0.89 kg/m; a 16 mm bar about 1.58 kg/m.

faq.q: How many rebar pieces do I need for my project?
faq.a: Divide the total rebar length by the stock bar length you buy (12 m for Indian TMT) and round up. The calculator does this automatically and shows the pieces count.

faq.q: Do I need rebar in a footing or foundation?
faq.a: Almost always yes. Footings and foundations carry the full building load and need reinforcement against bending and cracking. Typical guidance: 150–200 mm c/c with 12–16 mm bars in the top and bottom meshes. Confirm against your structural drawings.

faq.q: Do I need rebar in a concrete wall?
faq.a: It depends. Retaining and foundation walls almost always need vertical rebar plus horizontal distribution bars. Simple partition walls may only need light mesh. Set the member to "wall" and confirm with an engineer.

Edge cover is the distance from the outermost rebar line to the concrete edge — the concrete around the bars that protects them from water and corrosion. The calculator subtracts two edge covers (one per end) from each dimension to get the actual grid size.

It is the total rebar weight divided by the member area — a quick density check for an estimate. A single-layer 150 mm c/c 12 mm mesh is about 11–12 kg per m²; a double mesh with 16 mm bars can reach 20–25 kg per m².
